key_points.point_text: Canon is manufactured by money, luck, exposure, not pure quality, and taste itself was manufactured (one of many possible canons).
key_points.evidence_quote: Cultural canons are manufactured by money and luck amplifying exposure, with quality only a loose filter. ... reshuffled patronage yields an almost entirely different canon ... Taste itself was manufactured
key_points.reasoning: Summary line states the thesis explicitly; L035 and L039 supply the alternate-canon and manufactured-taste components.

key_points.point_text: Forgotten scale: 200 to 500 Viennese composers, 3,400 IMSLP Classical-era composers, several hundred on Wikipedia, fewer than 20 remembered.
key_points.evidence_quote: We remember fewer than 20 of 200 to 500 Viennese contemporaries and 3,400 catalogued composers.
key_points.reasoning: Captures Viennese range, the 3,400 catalogue figure, and fewer than 20, but drops the 'Wikipedia lists several hundred' number. Must-have point with a dropped number is at most Partial.

key_points.point_text: History cannot be replayed, so the author simulated cultural markets and ran it thousands of times to test whether remembered composers were best or merely well-positioned.
key_points.evidence_quote: History cannot rerun, but a model of cultural markets can run thousands of times. ... Author built a simulation; formal paper linked
key_points.reasoning: Both the impossibility of rerunning and the simulation-as-substitute with thousands of runs are stated.

key_points.point_text: Three hypotheses: Cream Rises, Money Writes History, Floors and Ceilings, with Story 3 the conclusion.
key_points.evidence_quote: Three hypotheses compete: cream rises, money writes, floors and ceilings.
key_points.reasoning: All three stories are listed with their content, and L029/L010 establish Floors and Ceilings as the landing point.

key_points.point_text: Three mechanisms combined: mere exposure, social influence, cumulative advantage (Matthew Effect, Robert Merton).
key_points.evidence_quote: Three documented mechanisms combine: mere exposure, social influence, cumulative advantage. ... Matthew effect magnifies small differences
key_points.reasoning: All three mechanisms and the Matthew effect are named. Merton's attribution is absent but the substantive content of the mechanism is intact.

key_points.point_text: Mere exposure: Zajonc 1968, Bornstein 1989 meta-analysis of 208 experiments, r = 0.26, peaks then reverses with overexposure.
key_points.evidence_quote: Mere exposure (Zajonc 1968; Bornstein 1989, 208 experiments, r = 0.26) peaks then reverses.
key_points.reasoning: All names, year, experiment count, effect size, and the peak-then-reverse qualifier are preserved.

key_points.point_text: Salganik MusicLab 2006: 14,341 participants, 48 unknown songs, visible download counts or not, same song ranks 1st or 40th.
key_points.evidence_quote: Salganik MusicLab (2006): 14,341 listeners, 48 songs; same song ranked 1st or 40th.
key_points.reasoning: Study, year, participant count, song count, and rank instability are all captured; the visibility manipulation is implied by the social-influence framing at L021.

key_points.point_text: Model setup: three agent types (producers, consumers, gatekeepers); uncorrelated quality and capital; 1,000 producers, 10,000 consumers, ~2 min, 360+ runs, power analysis.
key_points.evidence_quote: Runs of 1,000 producers and 10,000 consumers, about 2 minutes each, 360+ per condition.
key_points.reasoning: Producer/consumer counts, runtime, and run count are intact, but the gatekeeper agent type and the formal power analysis are missing, narrowing the setup description.

key_points.point_text: Social influence weakens quality-success link: correlation drops significantly (p < 0.0001, 360 runs); mediocre early-lucky works ride social proof.
key_points.evidence_quote: With social influence visible, quality-success correlation drops (p < 0.0001, 360 runs).
key_points.reasoning: The significance value and run count are intact; the proxy-optimization nuance covers the mechanism by which luck converts to stardom.

key_points.point_text: Talent held constant, resources reshuffled over 200 runs, counterfactual distance 0.88 of 1; top 10 percent ~1 in 4 shot; 50th to 90th a lottery.
key_points.evidence_quote: Talent constant over 200 runs; reshuffled resources yield counterfactual distance 0.88 of 1. ... Only top 10% have a shot regardless of funding, even then only about 1 in 4
key_points.reasoning: All numbers and the percentile conclusions are preserved.

key_points.point_text: Four conditions: full 0.32, no social influence 0.35, equal capital 0.46, quality only 0.46; equalizing raises correlation 44 percent.
key_points.evidence_quote: Full model 0.32; no social influence 0.35; equal capital 0.46; quality only 0.46: equalizing adds 44%.
key_points.reasoning: All four correlations and the 44 percent gain are present, supporting the inference that capital gating outweighs herd behavior.

key_points.point_text: Stylized 18th-century Vienna model (300 composers, few patrons, strong word-of-mouth, no recording): distance 0.97, 2.5 percent of canonical composers shared.
key_points.evidence_quote: Stylized 1750 Vienna, 300 composers: distance 0.97, only 2.5 percent shared between histories.
key_points.reasoning: The distance and shared-percent numbers plus composer count survive, but the defining conditions (few wealthy patrons, strong word-of-mouth, no recording) are dropped, narrowing the scope.

key_points.point_text: Robustness: varying every parameter by 50 percent; most important factor is steepness of money-to-attention conversion (convex vs concave).
key_points.evidence_quote: Varying parameters ±50%: steep money-to-attention conversion sidelines quality.
key_points.reasoning: The parameter sweep and the centrality of the money-to-attention conversion steepness are captured; L028 illustrates the reach gap.

key_points.point_text: Highest-leverage intervention is wider exposure not better judgment: 1970s-80s blind auditions lifted women hires from 5 to 25 percent.
key_points.evidence_quote: Leverage is wider exposure; 1970s-80s blind auditions lifted women hires from 5% to 25%.
key_points.reasoning: The recommendation, era, and both percentages are intact, carrying the exposure-barrier conclusion.

key_points.point_text: Caveats: quality assumed real and stable (debatable); calibration from Salganik teenagers on pop songs over weeks generalizing to 18th-century aristocrats over decades; omits genre formation, critical discourse, tech change, cultural politics.
key_points.evidence_quote: Counterpoint: Quality as stable property is debatable; calibration leaps decades; genre and politics excluded.
key_points.reasoning: The core caveats appear, but the Salganik-teenagers-over-weeks calibration detail and the omitted critical discourse and technological change are dropped, so the caveat set is narrowed.

key_points.point_text: Bach-Bieber: analogy right on mechanism but wrong on quality floor; Bach excellent AND well-positioned; 20 to 50 equally great contemporaries unknown; mechanisms stronger today (hours vs decades).
key_points.evidence_quote: Bach was excellent AND positioned; reshuffled patronage yields an almost entirely different canon. ... Probably 20 to 50 equally great contemporaries stay unknown
key_points.reasoning: The floor-and-ceiling framing, the 'AND' verdict, the 20-to-50 estimate, and the faster modern mechanisms are all present.
